axes.title: GSPC SAFETY Axis — Top 10 Competitor/Peer Research
axes.intro: **Prepared for:** Council of AI (CSOAI) — neutral AI-governance measurement body **Axis:** SAFETY (jailbreak / refusal / security-safety — asisecurity.ai, rainbow testing, jail banks, sandboxes) **Date:** 2026-08-21 · **Researcher lane:** JEEVES (delegated subagent)

competitors.name: garak (NVIDIA)
competitors.what: Open-source LLM vulnerability scanner — probes hallucination, data leakage, prompt injection, misinformation, toxicity, jailbreaks. "nmap / Metasploit for LLMs."
competitors.adopt: Adopt its probe taxonomy + trigger/detector structure — label *why* a response failed (which probe category), like nmap output, instead of a flat pass/fail.

competitors.name: PyRIT (Microsoft)
competitors.what: Open-source AI red-teaming framework ("Python Risk Identification Tool for generative AI") — orchestrates attacks, scores, and stores results.
competitors.adopt: Adopt its orchestrator + persistent memory model — every probe in the Safety window is *scored and persisted* to a ledger (feeds our living DB → sim_emit_card), not just shown.

competitors.name: AILuminate (MLCommons)
competitors.what: Standardized LLM safety benchmark + public leaderboard — grades models on a set of hazard categories with a 5-point scale; now multimodal + jailbreak + agentic workstreams.
competitors.adopt: Adopt its 5-point grade scale + hazard taxonomy so the Safety window shows a standardized safety *grade badge* per hazard, plus its "hold the live set private to prevent contamination" discipline.

competitors.name: promptfoo
competitors.what: Open-source LLM eval + red-teaming framework — declarative YAML config, jailbreak/prompt-injection strategies, guardrails, CI/CD.
competitors.adopt: Adopt its declarative "redteam config" + named attack strategies — let the Safety window load a JSON attack plan and run named strategies (jailbreak, prompt-injection, RAG leakage) with assertions, CI-style.

competitors.adopt: Adopt a "scan before you probe" preflight — run a model/registry integrity scan (backdoored-weight / malicious-dependency signal) and show it *before* the jail-bank probe results.

adoptions: Run the jail banks from chat. Add a "Run jail bank" action in the chat window that executes curated banks — garak probes, HarmBench behaviors, JailbreakBench attacks — against a selected target, then renders the structured hitlog/report inline (garak's probe/detector + hitlog model is the reference). No separate CLI.

asisecurity checks (signed evidence). Wire every jailbreak run into the estate's Ed25519 sign/verify backbone (os.meok.ai/api/sign + /api/verify, referenced live by asisecurity.ai) so each run yields a signed, verifiable evidence pack — a *living attestation*, never a certification. The AG UI chat should emit a verify link + signature alongside every result.

Rainbow tests (multi-vector sweep). Adopt Giskard's scan()-style concurrent attack sweep plus PyRIT's multi-turn orchestration: run N jailbreak vectors simultaneously against the target and return a ranked severity issue list (worst-first), not a single pass/fail. This is the "rainbow" the operator wants to see at a glance.

The sandbox (hard isolation). Run all jail banks and probes in an isolated sandbox so a probe can never hit a production endpoint or exfiltrate data. Isolation is a first-class safety property of the chat window — the operator must be able to run the most hostile prompt-injection banks with confidence that the only target is the sandboxed model.

StrongREJECT-style rubric auto-scoring + signed ASR leaderboard. Use StrongREJECT/Inspect scorers to auto-grade each response as *refusal* vs. *harmful-compliance*, compute Attack Success Rate (ASR) per model/attack (JailbreakBench pattern), and publish signed leaderboard entries — turning one-off jailbreak chats into a continuously accumulating, verifiable measurement record.

axes.title: GSPC EFFICIENCY Axis — Competitor & Peer Research
axes.intro: **Scope:** cost / energy / compute efficiency measurement — the 20%-monitoring-overhead angle and "cheap deterministic verification."

competitors.name: MLPerf Power (MLCommons)
competitors.what: Optional power/energy dimension of the MLPerf Training/Inference benchmark suites. Measures energy consumed to accomplish a task (e.g. a training run) at node level, not just speed.
competitors.adopt: The calibrated measurement bar: report ≥1 sample/sec, max(run, 60 samples), and target ±5% accuracy at 1 Hz (SPEC/revenue-grade meter or an Olympic-scored comparison test). CSOAI's Efficiency window should state a numeri

competitors.name: Green Algorithms (green-algorithms.org, Cambridge)
competitors.what: Open-source carbon calculator for computational tasks; methodology by Lannelongue, Grealey & Inouye (2021, *Adv. Sci.*, DOI 10.1002/advs.202100707). Also Greencard + GA4H (health).
competitors.adopt: The "greencard" — a standardized, downloadable, self-contained summary badge for a single computation. CSOAI's window can emit a per-turn/per-query efficiency card (fits the existing 3KB signed-card format).

competitors.name: CodeCarbon (mlco2/codecarbon, codecarbon.io)
competitors.what: Python library to estimate & track CO₂ from local compute (CPU/GPU/TPU). MIT, open source (MILA / BCG GAMMA / Comet / Haverford lineage). For GenAI *API* calls it defers to EcoLogits.
competitors.adopt: Ultra-low-friction instrumentation — start/stop decorator + a zero-code CLI that wraps any command. The Efficiency window should auto-instrument with near-zero setup.

competitors.name: MLCO2 (mlco2.github.io/impact)
competitors.what: Early ML carbon estimator from Lacoste, Luccioni & Schmidt — *Quantifying the Carbon Emissions of Machine Learning* (NeurIPS 2019 Climate Change AI workshop, arXiv 1910.09700). Precursor to CodeCarbon.
competitors.adopt: The auto-generated, citation-ready disclosure block — one click produces a reproducible reporting snippet. CSOAI's window should offer "copy disclosure" output so any measurement is reportable.

competitors.name: MLCommons energy standardization / Power Working Group
competitors.what: The standards body behind MLPerf; its Power Working Group defines energy-measurement methodology and presents MLPerf Power (e.g. at IEEE HPCA, Mar 2025). Goal: comparable ML-system energy metrics.
competitors.adopt: Versioned, neutral rule governance — a frozen methodology that a community vets before any result is accepted. CSOAI (already neutral) should adopt the discipline of *freezing + versioning* the Efficiency axis method so

competitors.name: Hugging Face AI Energy Score
competitors.what: Standardized energy-efficiency rating for AI model inference across 10 common tasks, all benchmarked on NVIDIA H100; reports GPU energy in Watt-hours; rates 1–5 stars (20% bands); open + proprietary models; leaderboard r
competitors.adopt: Fixed-hardware, banded rating — normalize to one reference hardware, measure *energy* (Wh) not emissions, and map to a 1–5 star band. CSOAI can anchor its Efficiency score to a fixed reference class + time-stamped band s

competitors.name: EDP — Energy–Delay Product (metric, not a single tool)
competitors.what: A figure of merit, not a product: Energy × Delay (and Energy × Delay²), descended from the digital-electronics Power–Delay Product (PDP = power × delay = switching energy per event). Widely used in accelerator/TinyML/MLP
competitors.adopt: Combine energy AND latency into one figure of merit (EDP) — so a fast-but-thirsty model can't hide behind a slow-but-frugal one. The Efficiency window should show J, s, and J·s together.

competitors.name: WattTime (marginal-emissions data; now under RMI)
competitors.what: Nonprofit marginal emissions data provider: API v3 serving MOER (marginal operating emissions rate) + signals like co2_moer and health_damage, enabling automated emissions reduction (AER) — shift compute to cleaner times
competitors.adopt: Marginal (not average) carbon signal + forecast — show gCO₂/kWh *now vs. later* so the user can defer a heavy job to a cleaner window; distinguish marginal from average grid intensity.

competitors.name: LangSmith (LangChain) / Langfuse — LLM cost & latency traces
competitors.what: LLM observability platforms that trace every call and attribute tokens, cost, and latency per trace. Langfuse is open source (MIT, YC W23); LangSmith is LangChain's commercial platform.
competitors.adopt: Zero-config per-call cost/latency attribution with a built-in model price table. The Efficiency window should auto-tag every chat turn with tokens/cost/latency and aggregate by model + axis.

competitors.name: Kepler (CNCF sandbox)
competitors.what: Kubernetes-based Efficient Power Level Exporter — a Prometheus exporter that measures energy consumption at container / pod / node level in K8s clusters (Apache-2.0), attributing energy via system counters + ML power mod
competitors.adopt: Near-zero-overhead continuous telemetry via an exporter/sidecar — sample system counters instead of instrumenting every call. This is the direct answer to the 20%-monitoring-overhead requirement.

adoptions: A deterministic, calibrated measurement bar (from MLPerf Power). Stop showing uncalibrated estimates as if they were measurements. Adopt a stated bar — sample ≥1 Hz, max(run, 60 samples), target ±5% accuracy — and render every figure with an explicit measured | estimated | reference tag plus its accuracy/confidence. Cheap deterministic verification comes from *declaring the meter's own error*, not

A combined Energy–Delay figure of merit (from EDP). Show J, seconds, and J·s (EDP) for every run, never energy alone. This closes the gaming path where a fast-but-thirsty model outscores a frugal-but-slow one (and vice-versa), and gives the Efficiency axis a single comparable number that already respects the "efficiency = cost × time" definition.

Fixed-reference, banded star rating (from Hugging Face AI Energy Score). Anchor efficiency to a declared reference hardware class, measure energy (Wh), not emissions, and map results to a 1–5 star band with a timestamp (bands are relative and must be re-anchored each round). This keeps comparisons apples-to-apples and lets the window show *efficiency* independent of grid location, while a separate

Marginal, time-aware carbon signal (from WattTime). Add a marginal carbon intensity readout (gCO₂/kWh, current + short forecast) alongside the flat grid-average number, and let the user see "run now vs. run in 2h" before dispatching a heavy job. Marginal ≠ average, and showing both is the honest, decision-useful framing for a cost/energy window.

Zero-config auto-instrumentation + per-turn tags + a signed efficiency card (from CodeCarbon + Langfuse + Green Algorithms). Instrument with a start/stop decorator and a zero-code CLI wrapper (CodeCarbon); auto-tag every chat turn with tokens / cost / latency / energy and aggregate by model + axis using a built-in model price table (Langfuse); then emit a small signed "efficiency card" per turn or

axes.title: GSPC CREATIVITY Axis — Top-10 Competitor/Peer Learning
axes.intro: **Prepared for:** Council of AI (CSOAI) · AG UI Creativity chat window **Scope:** generative novelty/creativity measurement — divergence vs convergence, originality scoring **Honesty note:** research-only; every claim below was verified against the cited source via web_search + curl (live pages / arXiv / ACL Anthology / GitHub API). Where a named "suite" is a loose category rather than a single canonical artifact, that is flagged explicitly rather than overstated. No accounts, no submissions.

competitors.name: Divergent Association Task (DAT) — Jay Olson (PNAS 2021)
competitors.what: 4-minute verbal-creativity test: name 10 unrelated nouns; score = mean pairwise semantic distance between words
competitors.adopt: Percentile-ranked divergence gauge + "first score only" anti-gaming rule — score the user's idea-spread against a norm, but hide the distance breakdown until the round closes

competitors.name: AUT (Alternative Uses Test) automation — Acar/Organisciak/Dumas/Beaty
competitors.what: Automates scoring of the classic Guilford AUT (list alternative uses for an object) with LLMs + semantic distance
competitors.adopt: **Fluency / flexibility / originality triple, where originality = semantic distance from the *crowd* of common answers** — score each user idea against the distribution of typical responses, not just internally

competitors.name: Torrance TTCT digitisation (figural CV scoring) — Acar & Organisciak
competitors.what: Digitises/scales the Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking (figural form) via computer-vision scoring of fluency/originality/elaboration
competitors.adopt: **Treat machine scoring as *attestation*, never autonomous certification** — CSOAI's existing "Living Attestation, never Living Certification" stance is exactly right here; show a confidence/validation flag on any auto-s

competitors.name: Semantic-distance / novel-object originality metrics — Dumas & Dunbar et al.
competitors.what: Originality as distributional semantics: an idea is original if semantically distant from the set of typical responses (LSA/word-vector cosine)
competitors.adopt: **Decouple fluency (volume) from originality (distance) as *separate* scores** — two ideas at equal count can differ hugely in novelty; never report a single blended number

competitors.name: ML creativity benchmarks — FOCUS, CreativeBench
competitors.what: Automated LLM creativity eval: FOCUS measures/cuts self-plagiarism; CreativeBench scores code creativity as quality×novelty with self-play
competitors.adopt: Unified metric = quality × novelty (not additive), with an executable/verifiable ground-truth check — so "creative" can never hide hallucination; CreativeBench's "larger = more correct but *less divergent*" is a real ris

competitors.name: Poetry / StoryGen originality evals — "Who Wrote This Line?" et al.
competitors.what: Detects / scores originality of generated poetry & stories (classical + modern Chinese poetry, authorship detection)
competitors.adopt: Show a "machine-authorship / memorisation risk" indicator on poetic/story output — flag lines that echo training data or fall into detectable style templates, separate from pure novelty

competitors.name: Creative Problem Solving (CPS) evals — RAT / insight / convergent-divergent batteries
competitors.what: Convergent + divergent thinking batteries (Remote Associates Test, insight problems); now used to benchmark AI vs humans
competitors.adopt: Report BOTH a convergent (correct/solve) and a divergent (idea-spread) channel in the chat window — the axis is "creativity", not "correctness"; label which is which

competitors.name: Originality detectors — self-BLEU / FQ-Eval / RiddleScore
competitors.what: Measure how much generated text is genuinely novel vs self-repeated or corpus-echoed (n-gram self-overlap, rejection-based originality filters)
competitors.adopt: Live "novelty strip": distinct-n + self-BLEU + corpus-overlap shown inline, so users see originality as a *measurable property of the text*, not a vibe

competitors.name: Semantic novelty metrics (cross-domain)
competitors.what: Embedding-based novelty/diversity: cosine distance to nearest known artifact, semantic divergence within a set, dimension-scaled novelty
competitors.adopt: Nearest-neighbour "distance-to-known" novelty — score each user/AI idea by how far it sits from the nearest already-seen artifact, with a constructive (not just divergent) framing

competitors.name: "9-creativity-benchmarks" suites (holistic multi-task) — AGC-Bench, CreativityPrism
competitors.what: *Honesty flag: no single canonical artifact named exactly "9 creativity benchmarks" verified.* The real, verified equivalents are holistic multi-task suites: AGC-Bench (systematic review → 78 datasets / 6 domains, first
competitors.adopt: **Multi-dimensional taxonomy (quality / novelty / diversity) with an open-weight *calibrated* judge and a public percentile leaderboard** — and report novelty SEPARATELY because it correlates poorly with the other axes

adoptions: Real-time semantic-distance divergence gauge, percentile-ranked, "first score only" (from DAT).
Split the axis into two explicit channels: DIVERGENCE vs CONVERGENCE, and surface "convergence-by-scaling" (from CreativeBench + CPS evals).
Score novelty as QUALITY × NOVELTY with a verifiable/executable check (from CreativeBench + FOCUS).
Live originality strip: distinct-n + self-BLEU + corpus overlap + self-plagiarism penalty (from FOCUS + originality detectors).
Open-weight calibrated judge + percentile norms, multi-dimension report (from AGC-Bench + CreativityPrism).

axes.title: SOVEREIGNTY Axis — Competitor/Peer Research (GSPC)
axes.intro: **Axis:** Sovereignty — user control, opt-out, no lock-in, data portability (GDPR Art 20), the ability to leave a system cleanly. **Scope:** Top 10 competitors/peers for the SOVEREIGNTY axis. **Method:** `web_search` + `curl` against primary sources (EUR-Lex, W3C/Solid, spec.c2pa.org, Google/Mastodon/Ollama/Inrupt docs). **Verified claims only**; each row cites the source actually fetched. Research only — no accounts, no submissions. **Date:** compiled 2026.

competitors.name: GDPR Art 20 — Right to data portability
competitors.what: Legal right to receive personal data "provided to a controller" in a *structured, commonly used, machine-readable format* and transmit it to another controller *without hindrance*; direct controller→controller transfer "
competitors.adopt: The predicate form: express sovereignty as machine-checkable conditions (format = machine-readable, hindrance = false, direct_transfer = feasible).

competitors.name: Solid Pods / Inrupt (ESS)
competitors.what: Decentralized data ownership: data lives in a Pod the user controls, shared on their terms. W3C Solid Protocol 0.11.0 = "secure and permissioned access to externally stored data in an interoperable way." Inrupt's Enterpr
competitors.adopt: Identity↔storage decoupling: separate the identity from the data store so "leaving" is a Pod/WebID move, not a rewrite.

competitors.name: Mastodon / ActivityPub federation exit
competitors.what: Fediverse account migration: export your social graph, redirect/move your identity across instances (ActivityPub Move), and delete cleanly.
competitors.adopt: One-click "leave" affordance with explicit redirect-vs-move semantics and a cooldown safety check.

competitors.name: Google Takeout (data-export pattern)
competitors.what: Reference data-export tool: per-product export → archive → deliver. Explicitly notes download ≠ delete.
competitors.adopt: Export ≠ deletion disclosure, plus per-scope selection granularity (choose exactly what leaves).

competitors.name: Self-hosted AI — Ollama portability
competitors.what: Local open-weight models, no API lock-in. Models are open-weight (GGUF/llama.cpp lineage), run locally, pullable/redistributable; REST API on :11434.
competitors.adopt: Open-weight + standard-format = no lock-in: assert "weights are exportable in an open format" as a sovereignty predicate.

competitors.name: C2PA provenance (rights portability)
competitors.what: Open standard for content authenticity: a tamper-evident manifest (claim + signed assertions + provenance chain of ingredients) that travels with the asset.
competitors.adopt: Signed manifest that travels with the exported data — make the portability result itself verifiable (CSOAI already ships signed h3k cards; extend the manifest to carry portability predicates).

competitors.name: No-lock-in contract clauses (EU Data Act Ch. VI)
competitors.what: Mandatory switching rights for data-processing services: contract must state switching rights, allow porting exportable data + digital assets, achieve *functional equivalence* after exit, unbundle services; switching cha
competitors.adopt: Exit-contract check: verify a switching clause + "no egress charge" + "functional equivalence on exit" exist before sign-up.

competitors.name: DSP (Dataspace Protocol) portability specs
competitors.what: Neutral protocol defining rules/procedures for publishing, negotiating, accessing data across platforms — data sovereignty via usage control. Now standardized (ISO-track; Eclipse Dataspace Protocol 2025-1).
competitors.adopt: Portable usage policy: attach the access/usage contract to the data itself, so control survives the transfer.

competitors.name: AI Act exit / withdrawal provisions
competitors.what: Statutory "off-switch" semantics: "recall" = return to provider / take out of service / disable use; "withdrawal" = prevent the system being made available on the market; plus Art 86 right to explanation for affected per
competitors.adopt: Enumerated exit verbs (recall = disable use; withdrawal = off-market) + a right to plain-language explanation of what leaving does.

competitors.name: EDPB portability guidance (WP29 WP242 rev.01)
competitors.what: Authoritative interpretation of Art 20 (WP29 guidelines, endorsed by EDPB): right is limited to data "provided by the data subject" (declared + observed), excludes inferred/derived data; machine-readable format required;
competitors.adopt: Scope honesty: surface the "provided-by-you vs derived-about-you" split and mark unverifiable items UNMEASURED, not silently "compliant".

adoptions: Portability predicates (machine-checkable, GDPR Art 20 + Data Act shaped)
Exit checks (one-click "leave" simulation, Mastodon + AI Act shaped)
No-lock-in verification (Solid + Ollama + Data Act shaped)
Signed, portable provenance + policy on the export (C2PA + DSP shaped)
Scope honesty + right-to-explanation in plain language (EDPB + AI Act Art 86 shaped)

axes.title: CARE Axis — Top 10 Competitors/Peers & What CSOAI Should Adopt
axes.intro: **GSPC axis:** CARE — AI that cares (duty-of-care, safety-of-care in health/social contexts, IEEE 7010 social impact). **Prepared for:** CSOAI (Council of AI) — AG UI "Care" chat window research. **Method:** Primary sources verified via `curl` (GOV.UK, WHO, NICE, CQC, IEEE, Nature Medicine, vendor sites, regulator/charity sites) plus `web_search`. Only claims corroborated by the fetched primary pages are asserted. No accounts created, no submissions made.

competitors.name: NHS AI and Digital Regulations Service (AIDRS)
competitors.what: A curated, single front-door for clinical/digital-health AI regulation and evaluation guidance, maintained jointly by NICE, MHRA, CQC and HRA, split into *developer* and *adopter* tracks.
competitors.adopt: The developer-vs-adopter split — the Care window should ask whether the user is *building* care AI or *using/choosing* it, and serve different duty-of-care guidance for each.

competitors.name: MHRA — Software & AI as a Medical Device (SaMD/AIaMD) + AI Airlock
competitors.what: UK statutory regulator for software/AI that is a medical device; assures safety via technical-file review, post-market surveillance, and a "Software and AI as a medical device change programme" plus the AI Airlock regula
competitors.adopt: Qualification/risk-gating question first — before answering, have the Care window help classify whether the subject is informational vs. a regulated medical-device use case, and refuse/redirect clinical decision-support

competitors.name: IEEE 7010-2020 — Well-being Impact Assessment (WIA)
competitors.what: The first international standard for assessing AI's impact on human well-being; a 5-activity, iterative, stakeholder-engaged impact-assessment methodology across 12 well-being domains.
competitors.adopt: The 12-domain well-being indicator dashboard — track a lightweight well-being baseline (affect, psychological/mental well-being, community/social support, health) over the conversation and across sessions.

competitors.name: NICE Evidence Standards Framework (ESF) for Digital Health Technologies
competitors.what: 21 evidence standards in 5 lifecycle groups that classify digital-health tech into risk-proportionate tiers (A/B/C) and define the evidence needed to deploy safely.
competitors.adopt: Risk-tiered response gating — classify the care topic by tier (informational / self-management / clinical decision-support) and vary evidence citation, disclaimers and cautions proportionately.

competitors.name: WHO — Ethics & governance of AI for health (2021) + LMM guidance (2024)
competitors.what: Global normative guidance: six core ethics principles (2021) and 40+ recommendations (2024) for governing large multi-modal models across five health applications.
competitors.adopt: A principles bar — surface the six care-ethics principles (protect autonomy, promote well-being, transparency, accountability, inclusiveness/equity, sustainability) as a persistent, checkable strip in the Care window.

competitors.name: HealthAI — The Global Agency for Responsible AI in Health
competitors.what: Geneva-based non-profit building national/regional validation mechanisms, a Global Regulatory Network (GRN), a Community of Practice (CoP), and a Global Directory of registered AI health solutions.
competitors.adopt: Co-production of a shared values statement — mirror HealthAI's "AI constitution"-style shared commitments as a one-line, user-visible care pledge in the window.

competitors.name: CQC — AI in health & social care
competitors.what: England's health/social-care regulator; sets out benefits, risks and "principles of good use of AI", and inspects providers so AI contributes to safe, effective, equitable, person-centred care (does not certify specific
competitors.adopt: Surface the de-personalisation/hallucination risks explicitly — the Care window should tell users plainly that AI can "hallucinate and present untrue information authoritatively as fact" and that human oversight can be n

competitors.name: **Mental-health AI auditing — SIM-VAIL (Oxford/UCL/AI Security Institute, *Nature Medicine* 2026)**
competitors.what: Clinically validated framework that simulates vulnerable users and stress-tests multi-turn chatbot behaviour, scoring exchanges across clinical risk dimensions and mapping "Vulnerability-Amplifying Interaction Loops" (VA
competitors.adopt: Multi-turn vulnerability monitoring, not single-message checks — detect and intervene at *early escalation points* (replacing one early concerning response improves the whole trajectory).

competitors.name: UK adult social-care AI governance — Digital Care Hub / AI in Social Care Alliance
competitors.what: Non-profit digital-care advisory body convening an action-focused Alliance to co-produce an "AI constitution for social care", practical provider guidance, training and case studies.
competitors.adopt: A co-produced, accessible "AI constitution" for the Care window — a short statement of care values and commitments the user can read and hold the tool accountable to.

competitors.name: Hippocratic AI — safety-focused healthcare LLM
competitors.what: Commercial safety-focused healthcare LLM with a proprietary multi-model "Polaris Constellation" architecture and a 5-phase safety certification (output testing, clinical supervision, escalation to human nurse, cross-vali
competitors.adopt: A visible escalation-to-human pathway — always offer a handoff to a real person/nurse for crisis or safety-critical care content (duty-of-care affordance).

adoptions: NHS AI and Digital Regulations Service (AIDRS)
MHRA — Software & AI as a Medical Device
NICE Evidence Standards Framework (ESF)
WHO — Ethics & governance of AI for health

axes.title: CSOAI AG UI — TRAINING Lane Competitive Research
axes.intro: **Scope:** AI-governance education/academy — turning the 16 measured GSPC axes into learnable material. **Method:** web_search + curl against primary sources. Verified claims only; sources cited inline. **Status:** Research-only. No accounts, no submissions, no paid content accessed.

competitors.name: ICO — Guidance on AI & data protection (UK regulator)

competitors.what: Free MOOC turning the 193-country-endorsed Recommendation on the Ethics of AI into practical learning.

competitors.name: NIST — AI Risk Management Framework + Playbook

competitors.adopt: "Governance = speed" reframe as the onboarding hook — position the Training lane as the accelerator, not the compliance tax.

competitors.what: Research institute producing governance analysis and *fostering talent* via fellowships rather than courses.

competitors.what: Vendor-neutral (CompTIA) and vendor (OneTrust) micro-credentials validating AI security/governance skills.
